newsitem.title: CHINA: HK banks to gain from cooler property market - KPMG.
newsitem.headline: HK banks to gain from cooler property market - KPMG.

text.p: Long-term banking stability in Hong Kong will benefit from efforts to cool an exuberant property market, KPMG Peat Marwick said on Wednesday.
In an annual survey of Hong Kong banks, it said banks' prospects hinged on macro-economic policies of the new Special Administrative Region (SAR) government, which took over Hong Kong on July 1.
"There has been talk of introducing a number of measures to curb the exuberant growth in the property market," Nick Etches, KPMG managing partner said.
"While these measures may in the short term dampen the prospects for the banking sector, they will contribute to the long-term stability of the sector," he said.
The survey found that the number of new mortgages granted in the second half of 1996 was 64,000, equal to the total for the whole of 1995.
The SAR government last week announced a boost in land supply in a bid to rein in property prices, and increase home ownership.
Growth in assets of banks in Hong Kong last year was almost three times higher than the economy as a whole, KPMG also said.
It said 1996 asset growth of Hong Kong authorised institutions was 13.6 percent, up from 10.9 percent in 1995.
This compared with a real growth in Hong Kong's gross domestic product of 4.7 percent, and inflation of 5.3 percent, the accounting firm said.
KPMG said it had found that foreign banks' fears over Hong Kong's return to China had subsided considerably.

"We have seen a number of foreign banks becoming more aggressive in gaining market share and increasing their Hong Kong asset base," said Paul Tsang, a senior partner in KPMG's banking and finance group.
